s: Where is the Space Applications Centre (SAC) of ISRO located?
x: SAC is at Ahmedabad; Bengaluru hosts URSC, ISTRAC and ISRO HQ, and NRSC is at Hyderabad.

s: In which State is the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC) at Mahendragiri located?
x: Mahendragiri is in Tamil Nadu; IPRC assembles and tests liquid and cryogenic engines and stages.

s: With which of the following is the Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad mainly associated?
x: SAC at Ahmedabad develops payloads for communication and remote sensing and undertakes applications research.

s: ISRO's Master Control Facility (MCF) for geostationary satellites has facilities at Hassan and which other place?
x: MCF operates from Hassan and Bhopal; ISTRAC at Bengaluru tracks launch vehicles and satellites.

s: Which ISRO centre handles satellite design and building?
x: URSC designs and builds satellites; VSSC handles launch-vehicle design and development.

s: Where is the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), which receives and distributes satellite data, located?
x: NRSC is at Hyderabad; its forerunner was NRSA.

s: What is the main work of the Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC), Bengaluru, opened on 30 January 2019?
o: Gaganyaan mission planning and crew training
x: HSFC handles Gaganyaan mission planning and crew selection and training.

s: For which of the following is the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC) of ISRO responsible?
x: LPSC develops liquid and cryogenic stages; URSC builds satellites and SAC makes payloads.

s: Which ISRO centre at Thiruvananthapuram is the lead centre for launch-vehicle design and development?
x: The Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), Thiruvananthapuram leads launch-vehicle design and development.

s: Which ISRO unit tracks launch vehicles and satellites through its telemetry, tracking and command network?
x: ISTRAC, Bengaluru runs ISRO's telemetry, tracking and command network.

s: What was the earlier name of the U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC), Bengaluru?
x: URSC was earlier the ISRO Satellite Centre (ISAC); it is named after U.R. Rao.

s: What was the forerunner of the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Hyderabad?
x: NRSC's forerunner was the National Remote Sensing Agency (NRSA).

s: Sriharikota, home of SDSC-SHAR, is now in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Sriharikota is now in Tirupati district; earlier it was in Nellore district.

s: The Solid Propellant Space Booster Plant (SPROB) at SDSC-SHAR is associated with the casting of which boosters?
o: Solid motors of sounding rockets only
x: SPROB is a major solid-propellant plant that casts the S200 boosters used in LVM3.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First launch pad — GSLV and LVM3
Second launch pad — PSLV and SSLV
First launch pad — PSLV and SSLV
Third launch pad — operational launch of PSLV-C62
x: C is correct: the first launch pad at Sriharikota handles PSLV and SSLV. A and B swap the pads (the second pad handles GSLV and LVM3 and is standby for PSLV). D is wrong: PSLV-C62 flew from the first launch pad; the Third Launch Pad is still to be built for NGLV.

s: Which of the following is NOT a reason supporting the selection of Sriharikota as a launch site?
o: Launches can proceed eastward over the sea.
The area is thinly populated and permits safe fall of spent stages.
The location benefits from the Earth's rotation.
It is located close to the northern polar region.
x: Sriharikota was selected because of its east-coast location, proximity to the equator, sea corridor for spent stages and relatively thin population. It is not close to the northern polar region.

s: For which launch vehicle is the Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota, approved on 16 January 2025, meant?
x: The Third Launch Pad (Rs 3,984.86 crore, 48 months) is for NGLV; the first pad serves PSLV and SSLV.

s:
Consider the following statements about SDSC-SHAR, Sriharikota:
1. Its First Launch Pad serves PSLV and SSLV.
2. Its public Launch View Gallery opened in 2019.
3. It was renamed after Satish Dhawan in 2012.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The First Launch Pad serves PSLV and SSLV and the gallery opened in 2019; SHAR was renamed after Dhawan in 2002, not 2012.

s: Sriharikota barrier island is situated between which of the following?
o: Kolleru Lake and the Arabian Sea
Pulicat Lake and the Bay of Bengal
Chilika Lake and the Indian Ocean
Vembanad Lake and the Bay of Bengal
x: Sriharikota lies between Pulicat Lake to the west and the Bay of Bengal to the east.

s: What was Sriharikota's launch centre called when it was set up in 1971?
x: It began in 1971 as the Sriharikota High Altitude Range (SHAR) and was renamed after Satish Dhawan in 2002.

s: Which mission marked the 100th launch from Sriharikota on 29 January 2025?
x: GSLV-F15 carrying NVS-02 (the 17th GSLV flight) was the 100th launch from SHAR.

s: What is the approved cost of the Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota, cleared on 16 January 2025?
x: The Third Launch Pad was approved at Rs 3,984.86 crore, to be built in 48 months.

s: Within how many months is the Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota to be completed?
x: The Third Launch Pad is to be built in 48 months; it will also be a standby for the second pad.

s: What is the main advantage of the Kulasekarapattinam launch complex for SSLV missions?
o: It is exclusively intended for launches of heavy-lift launch vehicles.
It permits direct southward launch into polar and sun-synchronous orbits without manoeuvring around Sri Lanka.
It is situated closer to the equator than Sriharikota and therefore eliminates all launch-cost constraints.
It enables launches directly into geostationary orbit without a cryogenic stage.
x: Kulasekarapattinam allows a direct southward trajectory into polar and sun-synchronous orbits, avoiding the fuel-costly manoeuvre around Sri Lanka required from Sriharikota.

s: The Kulasekarapattinam SSLV Launch Complex is in which district of Tamil Nadu?
x: It is in Thoothukudi (Tuticorin) district and is meant mainly for SSLV launches.

s: In which year was CSSTEAP, the UN-affiliated centre hosted at IIRS Dehradun, set up?
x: CSSTEAP dates from 1995; IIRS began in 1966 and IIST in 2007.

s: In which of the following fields does the Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS), Dehradun offer training?
x: IIRS trains in remote sensing, photogrammetry, cartography and geo-informatics/GIS; angiography and the other options are medical techniques.

s: The Indian Photo-interpretation Institute, founded in 1966, is now known as which of the following?
x: IIRS, Dehradun was founded in 1966 as the Indian Photo-interpretation Institute (IPI).

s: In which year was the Indian Institute of Remote Sensing founded, under its earlier name?
x: IIRS began in 1966 as the Indian Photo-interpretation Institute (IPI).

s: Where is CSSTEAP, the UN-affiliated Centre for Space Science and Technology Education in Asia and the Pacific, hosted?
x: CSSTEAP (1995) is hosted at IIRS, Dehradun.

s: Of which body is the Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS), Dehradun a constituent unit?
x: IIRS, Dehradun is a constituent unit of ISRO under the Department of Space.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS):
1. It offers training in cartography and geo-informatics.
2. Its field equipment includes a Linear Accelerator (LINAC).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: IIRS teaches remote sensing, photogrammetry, cartography and GIS; a LINAC is not part of its field equipment.

s: Where do ISRO's Space Technology Incubation Centres (STICs) mainly promote space-technology activities?
o: Universities in tier-2 and tier-3 cities
x: The six STICs promote space-technology activities in universities, particularly in tier-2 and tier-3 cities.

s: With which of the following is UNNATI associated?
x: UNNATI is a nanosatellite training programme established in 2018.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: RACS — Regional Academic Centres for Space
x: SpIN refers to the SpaceTech Innovation Network, launched in 2022. The school-student Young Scientist Programme is YUVIKA.

s: What is ISRO's YUVIKA (Yuva Vigyani Karyakram), started in 2019?
o: Young Scientist Programme for school students
x: YUVIKA is the Young Scientist Programme for school students; SPARK is the virtual museum and UNNATI the nanosatellite training.

s: How many Space Technology Cells (STC) has ISRO set up?
x: There are 9 Space Technology Cells, against 6 STICs and 6 Regional Academic Centres for Space.

s: What is SPARK, launched by ISRO on 10 August 2022?
x: SPARK is ISRO’s virtual space museum, launched on 10 August 2022.

s: What is the purpose of ISRO's RESPOND programme?
x: RESPOND funds space research in universities.

s: At which university is the Satish Dhawan Centre for Space Sciences located?
x: The Satish Dhawan Centre for Space Sciences is at the Central University of Jammu.

s: In which year was NSIL, the commercial arm of the Indian space sector, established?
x: NSIL was established in 2019; 1972 is the year ISRO came under the Department of Space.

s: The Chairman of ISRO also holds which of the following posts?
o: Chairman of IN-SPACe and CMD of NSIL
Secretary, Department of Space and Chairman, Space Commission
Scientific Adviser to the Prime Minister
x: The ISRO Chairman is also Secretary of the Department of Space and Chairman of the Space Commission; DoS works directly under the Prime Minister. IN-SPACe has its own chairman (Pawan Kumar Goenka) and NSIL is a separate CPSE; the AEC chairmanship belongs to the atomic energy set-up (Sarabhai held it after Bhabha in 1966, but it is not tied to the ISRO post); Scientific Adviser is not part of the role.

s: Where is IN-SPACe, set up in 2020 as an autonomous single-window space regulator, headquartered?
x: IN-SPACe, the single-window regulator set up in 2020, has its headquarters at Ahmedabad.

s: What is the status of India's comprehensive Space Activities Act as of 2026?
o: Was enacted with the Indian Space Policy 2023
x: As of 2026 India has no comprehensive Space Activities Act, though it has introduced policy and institutional reforms.

s: Which was the older commercial arm of the Department of Space, before NSIL was set up in 2019?
x: Antrix is the older commercial arm; NSIL (2019) is a CPSE; IN-SPACe is the regulator.

s: In which year did India adopt the Indian Space Policy?
x: The Indian Space Policy came in 2023, after NSIL (2019) and IN-SPACe (2020).

s: Who succeeded S. Somanath as Space Secretary and ISRO Chairman in January 2025?
x: V. Narayanan succeeded S. Somanath in January 2025.

s: Under whom does the Department of Space work directly?
x: DoS works directly under the Prime Minister; ISRO is a constituent of DoS.

s: Dr V. Narayanan, ISRO Chairman from 14 January 2025, is which Chairman of the organisation?
x: V. Narayanan is the 11th Chairman, succeeding S. Somanath (10th).

s: Who became ISRO Chairman on 15 January 2018, replacing A.S. Kiran Kumar?
x: K. Sivan, the 9th Chairman, served from 2018 to 2022.

s: Who was the second Chairman of ISRO, in 1972?
x: M.G.K. Menon briefly headed ISRO in 1972 between Vikram Sarabhai and Satish Dhawan.

s: Where are the headquarters of ISRO?
x: ISRO, a constituent of the Department of Space, is headquartered at Bengaluru.

s: Which of the following pairs (body – main function) is correctly matched?
o: National Atmospheric Research Laboratory — Atmospheric research
North Eastern Space Applications Centre — Microelectronics and chip fabrication
Semi-Conductor Laboratory — Space and planetary science
x: The National Atmospheric Research Laboratory (NARL), located at Gadanki, undertakes atmospheric research. The other functions are associated with PRL, NE-SAC and SCL respectively.

s: Where is the Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST) located?
x: IIST is at Thiruvananthapuram; Gadanki hosts NARL, Mohali the SCL and Shillong the NE-SAC.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SDSC SHAR – Sriharikota Deep Space Centre
APSAC – Andhra Pradesh Space Applications Centre
x: APSAC is the Andhra Pradesh Space Applications Centre. NSTL is the Naval Science & Technological Laboratory, NARL the National Atmospheric Research Laboratory and SDSC SHAR the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.

s: In which year was the Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology set up as a deemed university under the Department of Space?
x: IIST was established in 2007 as a deemed university under the DoS.

s: Where is the Andhra Pradesh Space Applications Centre (APSAC) located?
x: APSAC, for remote sensing and GIS, is at Vijayawada; NARL is at Gadanki and NSTL at Visakhapatnam.

s: What does the Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL) at Mohali mainly work on?
o: Space applications for the North East
x: SCL Mohali does microelectronics/chip fabrication; PRL does planetary science and NARL atmospheric research.

s: Where is NARL located?
x: NARL, the atmospheric research laboratory, is at Gadanki near Tirupati. Sriharikota hosts the SDSC SHAR launch centre.

s: Where is the North Eastern Space Applications Centre (NE-SAC) located?
x: NE-SAC, a DoS autonomous body, is at Umiam near Shillong in Meghalaya.

s: Where is the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) located?
x: PRL, founded by Vikram Sarabhai, is at Ahmedabad and works on space and planetary science.

s: Which institution is known as Asia's first space university?
x: IIST, Thiruvananthapuram, a deemed university under DoS set up in 2007, is Asia's first space university.

s: Where is the Naval Science & Technological Laboratory (NSTL) located?
x: NSTL is at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which of the following is NOT an overseas ISTRAC station?
x: Byalalu near Bengaluru hosts the Indian Deep Space Network; Mauritius, Brunei and Biak are overseas ISTRAC stations.

s: Where is the Indian Deep Space Network located?
x: The Indian Deep Space Network is at Byalalu near Bengaluru; Biak is an overseas ISTRAC station.

s: Under an ISRO-ESA Technical Implementing Plan, for which mission does ESA provide ground-tracking support?
x: The ISRO-ESA plan covers ground-tracking support for Gaganyaan.

s: Who was the Project Director of SLV-3?
x: Kalam directed the SLV-3 project; SHAR honours Satish Dhawan and URSC honours U.R. Rao.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with Vikram Sarabhai?
o: First ISRO Chairman until his death in 1971
Founder of the Physical Research Laboratory
Father of the Indian space programme
Founder of the Indian Deep Space Network at Byalalu
x: D is the mismatch: Sarabhai was the first ISRO Chairman until his death in 1971, founded PRL and is called the Father of the Indian space programme. The Indian Deep Space Network at Byalalu near Bengaluru is not among his foundations (PRL, IIM Ahmedabad, Darpana Academy, ATIRA).

s: Which of the following pairs (ISRO centre – person it is named after) is correctly matched?
x: URSC is named after U.R. Rao; SHAR honours Satish Dhawan and VSSC/TERLS honour Vikram Sarabhai.

s: Who conceived India's first satellite Aryabhata and the SITE experiment?
x: Vikram Sarabhai conceived Aryabhata and SITE; Satish Dhawan guided the programme through Aryabhata.

s: Which of the following institutions was NOT founded by Vikram Sarabhai?
x: Sarabhai founded PRL, IIM Ahmedabad, Darpana Academy and ATIRA, but not the Indian Deep Space Network.

s: Who founded the Darpana Academy and ATIRA at Ahmedabad?
x: Vikram Sarabhai founded PRL, IIM Ahmedabad, Darpana Academy and ATIRA.

s: Which satellite, launched by PSLV-C4 in 2002 as India's first full meteorological satellite, was later renamed Kalpana-I?
x: PSLV-C4 put METSAT (1,060 kg) into geosynchronous orbit in 2002; it was renamed Kalpana-I.

s: Which launch vehicle launched EOS-05, India's first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit?
x: GSLV-F17 placed EOS-05 into a sub-GTO on 4 September 2026.

s: Chandrayaan-3 was launched by which of the following?
x: Chandrayaan-3 was launched by LVM3-M4 in July 2023.

s: Which launch set the record for the largest number of satellites in a single Indian launch?
x: PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites in February 2017, establishing the multi-satellite record stated here.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about GISAT-1?
o: It was successfully placed in its intended orbit.
x: GISAT-1 was lost because GSLV-F10 suffered a cryogenic-stage anomaly, so it never reached orbit.

s: Which launch vehicle launched SpaDeX on 30 December 2024?
x: SpaDeX flew on PSLV-C60 and docked on 16 January 2025, making India the fourth docking nation.

s: Which launch vehicle launched Aditya-L1 on 2 September 2023?
x: Aditya-L1 flew on PSLV-C57 (XL); LVM3-M4 carried Chandrayaan-3.

s: Which satellite did PSLV-C48 (11 December 2019), the 50th PSLV flight, carry?
x: PSLV-C48 carried RISAT-2BR1 and 9 foreign satellites; Cartosat-3 flew on PSLV-C47.

s: Which launch vehicle carried GSAT-6A (March 2018), with which contact was lost after launch?
x: GSAT-6A flew on GSLV-F08; GSLV-F10 carried GISAT-1.

s: Which launch vehicle launched NVS-02 on the 100th launch from Sriharikota?
x: NVS-02 flew on GSLV-F15; a valve malfunction stopped it reaching its intended orbit.

s: PSLV-C55, which launched TeLEOS-2 and Lumelite-4 on 22 April 2023, was which PSLV mission?
x: PSLV-C55 on 22 April 2023 was the 57th PSLV mission.

s: Which launch vehicle launched NISAR on 30 July 2025, becoming the first GSLV to reach a sun-synchronous polar orbit?
x: GSLV-F16 launched NISAR, the first GSLV mission to a sun-synchronous polar orbit.

s: Which launch vehicle launched Chandrayaan-2 in 2019?
x: Chandrayaan-2 flew on GSLV Mk III-M1 (LVM3-M1); Chandrayaan-3 flew on LVM3-M4.

s: Which Indian launch vehicle launched the OneWeb satellites?
x: LVM3-M2 and LVM3-M3 launched 72 OneWeb satellites in total.

s: How many OneWeb satellites in all did LVM3-M2 and LVM3-M3 launch?
x: The two LVM3 missions together launched 72 OneWeb satellites.

s: Which launch vehicle launched BlueBird Block-2 (6,100 kg), the heaviest payload from Indian soil?
x: LVM3-M6 lifted BlueBird Block-2 on 24 December 2025; the older record was INSAT-4CR on GSLV-F04.

s: PSLV-C62 (12 January 2026), which failed at its third stage, was which PSLV flight?
x: PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 was the 64th PSLV flight and failed at the third stage.

s: GSLV-F15, the 100th launch from Sriharikota, was which flight of the GSLV?
x: GSLV-F15/NVS-02 (29 January 2025) was the 17th GSLV flight.

s: Which PSLV mission, launched on 18 May 2025, failed at its third stage?
x: PSLV-C61/EOS-09 (18 May 2025) and PSLV-C62 both failed at the third stage.

s: BlueBird Block-2, the heaviest payload launched from Indian soil, belongs to which company?
x: BlueBird Block-2 (6,100 kg) of AST SpaceMobile, USA, was launched by LVM3-M6 on 24 December 2025.

s: Which generation of Indian launch vehicle is GSLV?
x: PSLV is the third-generation vehicle and GSLV the fourth-generation.

s: ASLV was an all-solid launch vehicle with how many stages?
x: ASLV had five solid stages; SLV-3 had four.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about GSLV Mk II?
o: Its first stage uses HTPB solid propellant.
Its third stage is cryogenic, using LH2 and LOX.
Its second stage uses a Vikas engine with UH25 and N2O4.
x: GSLV Mk II has four liquid strap-ons, not two solid ones.

s: Which of the following is the configuration of LVM3?
o: Four solid stages followed by a Vikas liquid stage
Two S200 solid strap-ons, an L110 liquid core and a C25 cryogenic stage
Three solid stages and a liquid velocity-trimming module
HTPB first stage, UH25 second stage and CE-7.5 third stage
x: LVM3 uses two S200 solid strap-ons, an L110 liquid core and a fully indigenous C25 cryogenic stage.

s: What does SSLV consist of?
o: Four stages in a solid-liquid-solid-liquid sequence
One solid, one liquid and one cryogenic stage
Three solid stages and a liquid Velocity Trimming Module
x: SSLV has three solid stages and a liquid Velocity Trimming Module that provides precise orbit insertion.

s: What is the order of PSLV's four stages?
x: PSLV is solid-liquid-solid-liquid with no cryogenic stage; it was the first Indian launch vehicle with liquid stages.

s: What stages did SLV-3, India's first satellite launch vehicle, have?
o: Three solid stages and a VTM
x: SLV-3 had 4 all-solid stages; ASLV had 5 and SSLV has 3 solid stages plus a VTM.

s: What is the full form of PSLV?
x: PSLV stands for Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, ISRO's 'workhorse'.

s: Which Indian launch vehicle is nicknamed 'Bahubali'?
x: LVM3, formerly GSLV Mk-III, is called 'Bahubali' as India's heaviest launcher.

s: Which was the first Indian launch vehicle to have liquid stages?
x: PSLV was the first Indian vehicle with liquid stages; SLV-3 and ASLV were all-solid.

s: Which launch vehicle serves SSO, LEO and GTO missions, including Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission?
x: PSLV serves SSO, LEO and GTO and launched Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission.

s: Which launch vehicle is mainly used to place 2-2.5 tonne communication and navigation satellites into GTO?
x: GSLV Mk II is designed to place 2–2.5 tonne communication and navigation satellites into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit.

s: About how much payload can LVM3 carry to GTO and LEO respectively?
o: 8 tonnes to GTO and 4 tonnes to LEO
4 tonnes to GTO and 8 tonnes to LEO
2 tonnes to GTO and 4 tonnes to LEO
500 kg to GTO and 1,750 kg to LEO
x: The stated LVM3 capacity is about 4 tonnes to GTO and 8 tonnes to LEO, although some descriptions cite approximately 10 tonnes to LEO.

s: PSLV can place about how much payload into Sun-synchronous orbit?
x: PSLV carries about 1,750 kg to SSO and about 1,425 kg to GTO.

s: Where is a second spaceport for SSLV launches being established?
x: Orbital launches, including private Agnibaan missions, take place from Sriharikota; a second SSLV spaceport is coming up at Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu.

s: LVM3 ended India's dependence on foreign launchers for placing satellites of about what mass into GTO?
x: LVM3 can place about 4 tonnes into GTO and ended India's dependence on foreign launchers for 4-tonne satellites.

s: SSLV, with three solid stages, can place about 500 kg into a LEO of about what height?
x: SSLV places about 500 kg into a 500 km LEO; SSLV-D1 failed, while D2 and D3 succeeded.

s: Which company won the ₹511 crore Transfer of Technology agreement to build and operate SSLV independently?
x: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) won the ₹511 crore SSLV Transfer of Technology agreement. It was described as the first full Transfer of Technology of an ISRO launch vehicle to industry.

s: For what is SSLV mainly designed?
o: Low-cost, launch-on-demand launches of small satellites
x: SSLV is a low-cost, launch-on-demand vehicle for satellites of up to 500 kg to 500 km LEO.

s: What happened on the first SSLV flight, SSLV-D1 (August 2022)?
o: Placed EOS-02 in its intended orbit
Was a suborbital test without a satellite
Failed to place EOS-02 in its intended orbit
x: SSLV-D1 failed to reach the intended orbit; SSLV-D2 (2023) and D3 (2024) succeeded.

s: Which PSLV variant is correctly matched with its number of strap-on motors?
x: PSLV-QL has four strap-ons; PSLV-CA has zero, PSLV-DL two and PSLV-G six.

s: Which was the first sounding rocket launched from Thumba?
x: The first sounding rocket launched from Thumba was the American Nike-Apache on 21 November 1963.

s: Why was Thumba selected for the establishment of TERLS?
o: It lies close to the international date line
It is located near the Baikonur Cosmodrome
The geomagnetic equator passes through it
x: Thumba was selected because the geomagnetic equator passes through the location, making it suitable for sounding-rocket experiments.

s: For what are Rohini sounding rockets mainly used?
o: Geostationary communication and television broadcasting only
Atmospheric research and qualification of launch-vehicle subsystems
x: Rohini sounding rockets carry payloads for atmospheric research and are also used to test and qualify systems intended for larger launch vehicles.

s: In the Rohini sounding-rocket names RH-200, RH-300 and RH-560, what does the number indicate?
x: The number in an RH designation denotes the rocket diameter in millimetres.

s: When did RH-200 achieve the 200th consecutive successful launch from Thumba?
x: RH-200 completed its 200th consecutive successful launch from Thumba in November 2022.

s:
Match the following early sounding rockets used at Thumba with their country of origin:
List-I
A. Nike-Apache
B. M-100
C. Centaure
List-II
1. France
2. USA
3. Russia
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Nike-Apache was American, M-100 Russian and Centaure French; indigenous rockets came from 1965.

s: Which Indian launch vehicle made its first flight in 1987?
x: First flights: SLV-3 (1979), ASLV (1987), PSLV (1994), GSLV (2001).

s: Which of the following launch vehicle – first successful payload pairs is correctly matched?
x: PSLV's first successful payload was IRS-P2; SLV-3's was Rohini RS-1 and GSLV's first payload was GSAT-1.

s: What was CARE, launched by LVM3 on 18 December 2014?
x: CARE was a suborbital experimental payload launched by LVM3 on 18 December 2014.

s: The first successful flight of PSLV (D2, 15 October 1994) placed which satellite in orbit?
x: PSLV-D2 carried IRS-P2; Rohini RS-1 flew on SLV-3 and GSAT-1 on GSLV-D1.

s:
Which is the correct chronological order of the first flights of the following launch vehicles?
1. LVM3
2. ASLV
3. SSLV
4. GSLV
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Which satellite did GSLV carry on its first flight (GSLV-D1) on 18 April 2001?
x: GSLV-D1 (18 April 2001) carried GSAT-1, weighing 1,536 kg.

s: In which year did ASLV have its first successful flight?
x: ASLV failed in 1987 and 1988 and first succeeded in 1992 with the SROSS series.

s: What level of automatic FDI do the current rules permit in launch vehicles and spaceports?
x: The revised rules allow 49% automatic FDI in launch vehicles and spaceports.

s: Which company built Vikram-S ('Prarambh'), India's first private rocket launched on 18 November 2022?
x: Vikram-S was built by Skyroot of Hyderabad and was a suborbital flight.

s: Agnikul Cosmos' Agnibaan SOrTeD (30 May 2024) used which 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine?
x: Agnibaan used the 3D-printed Agnilet semi-cryogenic engine; Kalam-250 is a Skyroot stage.

s:
Consider the following statements about Skyroot's rockets:
1. Vikram-S reached orbit in 2022.
2. Vikram-1 was the first privately developed Indian rocket to reach orbit.
3. The Kalam series are the solid stages of Vikram-1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Vikram-1 reached orbit in 2026 and uses the Kalam solid stages; Vikram-S was only suborbital.

s: How high did Skyroot's Vikram-S ('Prarambh') go on its suborbital flight of 18 November 2022?
x: Vikram-S reached 89.5 km; it was suborbital and the first IN-SPACe authorised launch.

s: Which company set up India's first private launchpad at Sriharikota?
x: Agnikul Cosmos launched Agnibaan SOrTeD (30 May 2024) from India's first private launchpad at Sriharikota.

s: By which year is the Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) meant to support India's crewed lunar landing goal?
x: NGLV is linked to the crewed lunar landing by 2040, not 2030; 2035 is the target for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about RLV-LEX?
o: It refers to autonomous landing tests of the Reusable Launch Vehicle Technology Demonstrator.
Its first test took place on 2 April 2023.
It was a cryogenic engine test for GSLV Mk-II.
The later reusable-vehicle landings of 2024 are called the 'Pushpak' landings.
x: RLV-LEX is a landing experiment, not an engine test.

s: Which launch vehicle is intended to carry Gaganyaan crew to approximately 400 km LEO for three days?
x: The human-rated LVM3, designated HLVM3, is intended for the Gaganyaan crew mission to a 400 km LEO orbit for three days.

s: Where were the autonomous landing tests of ISRO's RLV-TD 'Pushpak' (RLV-LEX) conducted?
x: RLV-LEX landing tests (2023-24) were held at Chitradurga; they were landing, not engine, tests.

s: Which reusable rocket made the first orbital-class booster landing on 21 December 2015?
x: Falcon 9 made the first orbital-class booster landing; New Shepard is a suborbital reusable rocket.

s: Which company developed New Shepard, a suborbital reusable rocket that landed in November 2015?
x: New Shepard is Blue Origin's suborbital reusable rocket; SpaceX's Falcon 9 made the first orbital-class booster landing.

s: When was the first Integrated Air Drop Test for Gaganyaan's human-rated LVM3 programme held?
x: The first Integrated Air Drop Test was held on 24 August 2025.

s: What is the full form of GTO in launch terminology?
x: GTO is the Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit, served by GSLV and LVM3; SSO is PSLV's speciality.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about orbits?
o: A geostationary orbit is a geosynchronous orbit over the equator.
Apogee is the point of an orbit nearest to the Earth.
GTO is an elliptical transfer orbit with its apogee near 36,000 km.
A geosynchronous orbit has a period of one day.
x: Apogee is the farthest point of an orbit; perigee is the nearest.

s: Why is a sun-synchronous satellite suitable for imaging?
o: always travels in an eastward equatorial orbit
passes over a given place at the same local solar time
x: A sun-synchronous orbit is generally near-polar and passes over a given location at approximately the same local solar time, which is useful for consistent imaging conditions.

s: Launch sites in which location gain the most fuel saving from an eastward launch?
x: Eastward launches gain Earth's rotational speed, and sites nearer the equator gain the most.

s: In which direction do polar and Sun-synchronous orbit launches from Sriharikota proceed, needing a dog-leg trajectory around Sri Lanka?
x: Polar and Sun-synchronous launches generally follow a southward trajectory from Sriharikota; a dog-leg is used to avoid Sri Lanka.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's cryogenic engine development?
o: Early GSLVs used Russian cryogenic engines.
Cryogenic technology transfer was denied to India in the 1990s.
India's own cryogenic engine first succeeded on GSLV-D1 in 2001.
GSLV-D5 (2014) was the first success of the indigenous cryogenic engine.
x: The first successful flight of India's own cryogenic engine was on GSLV-D5 in 2014, not GSLV-D1.

s: Where are engine tests for Indian cryogenic and semi-cryogenic systems conducted?
x: The tests are conducted at the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC), Mahendragiri, in Tamil Nadu. LPSC Valiamala is associated with design work and is not the testing facility identified here.

s: ISRO's SCE-200 semi-cryogenic engine, meant for the LVM3 upgrade and the NGLV, uses which propellant combination?
x: A semi-cryogenic engine burns refined kerosene with liquid oxygen; SCE-200 is meant for the LVM3 upgrade and NGLV. LH2 + LOX is the fully cryogenic combination (CE-7.5, C25); UH25 + N2O4 is the earth-storable Vikas combination; HTPB is a solid propellant.

s: Which stage does the CE-20 cryogenic engine power?
x: CE-20 (LH2 + LOX) powers LVM3's C25 stage; CE-7.5 powers the GSLV Mk-II upper stage.

s: What is the approximate specific impulse of cryogenic propulsion, the most efficient propellant category?
x: Cryogenic propulsion has an approximate specific impulse of 450 seconds, the highest among the propellant categories.

s: Where are cryogenic engines (liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen) mainly used?
o: Military missiles kept ready for long periods
x: Cryogenic propulsion is used in rocket upper stages (and was used on the space shuttle) because of its very high specific impulse (~450 s). Its low-density LH2 needs huge tanks and cannot be stored long, so it is unsuited to military missiles; attitude-control thrusters use hypergolic propellants that ignite on contact; sounding rockets use solid motors.

s: At about what temperature is liquid hydrogen stored in a cryogenic engine?
x: LH2 (the fuel) is stored at about -253°C and LOX (the oxidiser) at about -183°C; the exhaust is only water vapour.

s: What was the outcome of the 1991 Glavkosmos agreement concerning cryogenic technology?
o: Russia transferred all cryogenic technology without restriction.
The United States supplied seven cryogenic engines to India.
US MTCR-based sanctions stopped technology transfer, although Russia supplied seven engines.
The agreement was cancelled by India before any engines were supplied.
x: Glavkosmos agreed to sell engines and technology in 1991, but US MTCR-based sanctions in 1992 stopped technology transfer; Russia supplied seven engines only.

s: In which year did India's Cryogenic Upper Stage Project begin?
x: The project began in 1994 at a cost of ₹300 crore, and a full cryogenic stage was tested in 2006.

s: What does the Greek word 'Kryos', from which the term 'cryogenics' comes, mean?
x: Kryos means frost; cryogenics deals with temperatures below about -150°C.

s: With the indigenous CE-7.5 flying on GSLV-D5 in January 2014, India became which country to have cryogenic technology?
x: India is 6th, after the US, Russia, France, Japan and China - not 4th.

s: Cryogenic engines are unfit for military missiles mainly because liquid hydrogen:
o: Has very low density, needing huge tanks, and cannot be stored long
x: LH2 density is only 0.071 g/ml, so tanks are huge and storage is short - unsuited to missiles.

s: At about what temperature is liquid oxygen, the oxidiser of a cryogenic engine, kept?
x: LOX is at about -183°C; -253°C is the temperature of liquid hydrogen.

s: After the US MTCR sanctions of 1992, how many cryogenic engines did Russia supply to India?
x: The sanctions stopped technology transfer under the 1991 Glavkosmos deal, and Russia supplied only 7 engines.

s: Cryogenics deals with temperatures below about which level?
x: Cryogenics deals with temperatures below about -150°C, using liquid nitrogen, hydrogen and oxygen.

s: What is the only exhaust product of a cryogenic engine burning liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen?
x: LH2 + LOX burn to give only water vapour.

s: What is the significance of the CE-20 bootstrap-mode start test?
o: It eliminates the need for liquid oxygen in the engine.
It proves that CE-20 can operate only with solid propellant.
It demonstrates starting on the engine’s own propellant flow without external gas, supporting in-space restart.
It converts CE-20 into a hypergolic engine.
x: Bootstrap mode starts the engine using its own propellant flow without external gas and is important for in-space restart capability.

s: SE2000 is planned for which applications?
o: Replacing the C25 in GSLV Mk II only
The PSLV first stage and S200 booster only
Replacing the L110 in LVM3-SC and for the NGLV
x: SE2000 is planned for LVM3-SC, replacing the L110, and for the NGLV.

s: Which of the following ISRO engines is INCORRECTLY matched with its feature?
o: Vikas – UH25 + N2O4, PSLV second stage
CE-7.5 – LOX + LH2 staged-combustion engine, GSLV Mk II upper stage
CE-20 – 200 kN-class LOX + LH2 engine, LVM3 C25 stage
x: SE2000 is semi-cryogenic, using refined kerosene + LOX, not LOX + LH2.

s: The CE-7.5 cryogenic engine powers the upper stage of which launch vehicle?
x: CE-7.5 is the GSLV Mk II upper stage; CE-20 powers the LVM3 C25 stage.

s: Which ISRO engine uses UH25 + N2O4 and powers the L110 stage of LVM3?
x: Vikas burns UH25 + N2O4 and powers PSLV/GSLV second stages and the LVM3 L110.

s:
Consider the following statements about ISRO cryogenic engines:
1. CE-7.5 uses staged combustion and produces 75 kN.
2. CE-20 uses a gas-generator cycle and powers the LVM3 C25 stage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: CE-7.5 is a 75 kN staged-combustion engine; CE-20 is a 200 kN gas-generator engine on LVM3 C25.

s: Which propellants does the SE2000 semi-cryogenic engine use?
x: Semi-cryogenic means refined kerosene with liquid oxygen, not liquid hydrogen.

s: At what power level did the third hot test of the SE2000 semi-cryogenic engine's Power Head Test Article run in 2026?
x: The 2026 third hot test of the SE2000 Power Head Test Article was at 60% power.

s: Which propellant category is correctly matched with its characteristic?
o: Solid — high initial thrust but cannot normally be throttled or stopped
Hybrid — cannot be stopped or restarted
Hypergolic — requires an external ignition system at every start
Cryogenic — least efficient but simplest to handle
x: Solid propellants provide high initial thrust but generally cannot be throttled or stopped. Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact, hybrids can be stopped or restarted, and cryogenic systems are highly efficient but complex.

s: Which of the following is an earth-storable liquid propellant combination?
x: UH25 and N2O4 are listed as earth-storable liquid propellants. Refined kerosene and LOX are semi-cryogenic, while LH2 and LOX are cryogenic.

s: Why are hydrazine-family propellants combined with N2O4 called hypergolic?
o: Are non-toxic and suitable for large reusable boosters
Require cryogenic storage and have the highest specific impulse
Ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring
x: Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring, although they are highly toxic.

s: What does a hybrid rocket motor combine?
x: A hybrid uses solid fuel with a liquid oxidiser, so it can be stopped and restarted.

s: Which propellant category gives high initial thrust but cannot be throttled or stopped?
x: Solid motors such as HTPB in S200 cannot be throttled or stopped; hybrids can be stopped and restarted.

s: In solid rocket propellant, ammonium perchlorate acts as which of the following?
x: Ammonium perchlorate is the oxidiser; aluminium powder is the fuel and HTPB the binder.

s: Which substance is used as the fuel in solid rocket propellant along with ammonium perchlorate?
x: In solid propellant, aluminium powder is the fuel, ammonium perchlorate the oxidiser and HTPB the binder.

s: Who developed HSTDV, a scramjet vehicle?
x: HSTDV is DRDO's scramjet vehicle; DRDO has also tested an actively cooled full-scale scramjet combustor with an indigenous endothermic fuel.

s: Which air-breathing engine has supersonic combustion and is designed for about Mach 5–6 and above?
x: A scramjet burns fuel in supersonic airflow and is built for Mach 5–6+; a ramjet has subsonic combustion and works above Mach 2.

s: What is the main advantage of a scramjet over a conventional rocket during atmospheric flight?
o: It operates with subsonic airflow at speeds below Mach 2.
It eliminates the need for fuel during hypersonic flight.
It uses oxygen from the atmosphere, thereby reducing the weight of onboard oxidiser.
It uses a compressor to compress atmospheric air before combustion.
x: A scramjet uses oxygen from the atmosphere, so it need not carry the entire oxidiser required by a rocket. It still requires fuel and works with supersonic airflow.

s: With ISRO's ATV scramjet flight test (August 2016), India became which country to demonstrate scramjet flight?
x: India became the fourth country, after the US, Russia and China.

s: Which agency carried out the ATV scramjet flight test in August 2016?
x: ATV was ISRO's test from Sriharikota; HSTDV is DRDO's vehicle.

s: In May 2026, for how long did HSTDV's actively cooled full-scale scramjet combustor run on endothermic fuel?
x: DRDO's actively cooled full-scale combustor ran for 20 minutes.

s: In a ramjet engine, at what speed does the air flow during combustion?
o: Zero, as no air is used
x: A ramjet burns fuel in subsonic airflow; a scramjet burns it in supersonic airflow.

s: At what kind of system is ISRO's RLV-TD 'Pushpak', a reusable winged vehicle, aimed?
x: Pushpak is aimed at a TSTO system and has completed the LEX-03 autonomous landing experiment.

s: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of reusable launch systems?
o: Elimination of the need for thermal protection systems
Reduction in launch cost by up to 80 percent
x: Reusable vehicles require a reusable Thermal Protection System; its elimination is not a benefit identified for such systems.

s: By up to how much are reusable launch vehicles such as RLV-TD expected to cut launch cost?
x: Reusability is expected to cut launch cost by up to 80%.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ISRO's RLV-TD 'Pushpak'?
o: It aims at a TSTO vehicle
It does not need a thermal protection system
x: Pushpak needs a reusable Thermal Protection System; the other statements are correct.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the proposed NGLV 'Soorya'?
o: It is planned as a reusable heavy-lift rocket.
It is designed to carry about 10,000 kg to low Earth orbit.
Its projected LEO payload is about 2.5 times that of LVM3.
It is planned to use semi-cryogenic propulsion.
x: 'About 10,000 kg to LEO' is the wrong statement: the approved NGLV carries up to 30 tonnes to LEO (Cabinet, 18 Sep 2024), about three times LVM3, with a reusable first stage. Option c understates the ratio (about 3 times, not 2.5) but is not the intended answer.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: New Glenn is associated with Blue Origin. Falcon 9 and Starship belong to SpaceX, while Zhuque-3 belongs to LandSpace.

s: From which launch pad will NGLV 'Soorya' be launched?
x: Soorya is linked to the new Third Launch Pad; Dhanush is Agnikul's private pad.

s: Which company developed Zhuque-3, a reusable rocket?
x: Zhuque-3 is the reusable rocket of China's LandSpace.

s: NGLV 'Soorya' is designed to place how much payload in low Earth orbit?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (30,000 kg); it is added as option 5.
the 20,000 kg design figure was superseded — now 30 tonnes to LEO (Cabinet approval, 18 Sep 2024, IANS report)
The Cabinet approved NGLV on 18 Sep 2024 with a maximum payload of 30 tonnes to LEO and a reusable first stage, about three times LVM3. None of the printed figures is right; 20,000 kg was an earlier design figure.

s: To which company does the reusable rocket New Glenn belong?
x: New Glenn is Blue Origin's; Falcon 9 and Starship are SpaceX's, Zhuque-3 is LandSpace's.

s: To which company does the reusable rocket Falcon 9 belong?
x: Falcon 9, with over 520 booster recoveries, belongs to SpaceX.

s: Which propellants does SpaceX's fully reusable Starship use?
x: Starship is fully reusable and burns methane with liquid oxygen.

s: On which mission did Skyroot's Vikram-1 reach orbit as India's first private orbital rocket?
x: Vikram-1 (three solid stages + one liquid stage, 290 kg to 500 km SSO) reached orbit on Mission Aagaman.

s: For which of the following is Agnilet, developed by Agnikul Cosmos, known as the world's first?
x: Agnilet is described as the world’s first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.

s: Agnilet was flown in 2024 from which launch pad?
o: Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre’s private pad
Dhanush, India’s first private launch pad at Sriharikota
Satish Dhawan Space Centre’s second launch pad
A private launch pad at Bengaluru
x: Agnilet was flown in 2024 from Dhanush at Sriharikota, described as India’s first private launch pad.

s: EVEREST, unveiled by Astrobase in August 2026, is described as India’s first private:
o: 800 kN full-flow staged combustion LOX-methane engine
solid motor for the Agnibaan booster
x: Astrobase’s EVEREST is described as India’s first private 800 kN full-flow staged combustion LOX-methane engine.

s: Why is LOX-methane considered important for Mars-return missions and in-situ resource utilisation?
o: It can be stored indefinitely without refrigeration.
Methane can be produced from Martian resources, while the combination is cleaner and cheaper.
LOX-methane is a hypergolic combination that ignites on contact.
Methane has the highest density of all cryogenic fuels and needs no oxidiser.
x: LOX-methane is considered cleaner and cheaper, and methane can be produced from Martian resources.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: EVEREST is Astrobase's LOX-methane engine; Agnilet is Agnikul's, and KALAM 1200 and Vikram-1 are Skyroot's.

s: What is Skyroot's KALAM 1200, tested at SHAR?
x: KALAM 1200 is an 11 m, 30 t solid motor.

s: Agnite, the largest single-piece 3D-printed booster engine made of Inconel, was developed by which firm?
x: Agnikul Cosmos developed Agnite as well as the Agnilet engine.

s: How much payload can Skyroot's Vikram-1 place in a 500 km sun-synchronous orbit?
x: Vikram-1 has 3 solid and 1 liquid stage and can carry 290 kg to a 500 km SSO.

s:
Consider the following statements about ISRO's life-tested 300 mN Stationary Plasma Thruster:
1. It is a Hall-type thruster using xenon.
2. It is meant to replace chemical propulsion in the booster stages of future launch vehicles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the thruster will replace chemical propulsion on future communication satellites, not launch-vehicle boosters.

s: What is the role of the spent PS4 stage in POEM?
o: It is used as a planetary landing engine.
It is converted into a reusable crew capsule.
It is reused as an orbital platform for start-up and academic payloads.
It serves as a cryogenic upper stage for GSLV.
x: POEM reuses the spent PS4 stage as an orbital platform for start-up and academic payloads.

s: How long was the life test completed by ISRO's 300 mN Stationary Plasma Thruster?
x: The Hall-type xenon thruster passed a 1,000-hour life test.

s: What is the full form of POEM, which uses the spent PS4 stage as an orbital platform?
x: POEM = PSLV Orbital Experimental Module, hosting start-up and academic payloads.

s: Which start-up's RUDRA 0.3 HPGP green monopropellant thruster flew on POEM-3 of PSLV-C58 in January 2024?
x: RUDRA 0.3 HPGP, a green monopropellant thruster of Bellatrix Aerospace, flew on POEM-3 (PSLV-C58).

s: What kind of thruster is RUDRA 0.3 HPGP, demonstrated on POEM-3 in 2024?
x: RUDRA 0.3 HPGP is a green (non-toxic) monopropellant thruster for satellites.

s: What is the full form of APPLE, India's first experimental communication satellite launched in 1981?
o: Asian Public Platform for Long-distance Education
Aerial Payload and Propulsion Laboratory Experiment
x: APPLE stands for Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment, India's first experimental communication satellite (1981).

s: Where is the Master Control Facility that controls INSAT satellites located?
x: The MCF is at Hassan, Karnataka; INSAT is a joint venture of DoS, DoT, IMD, AIR and Doordarshan coordinated by the ICC.

s: INSAT-4C was lost in 2006 when which launch vehicle failed?
x: INSAT-4C was lost on GSLV-F02 (2006); its replacement INSAT-4CR flew on GSLV-F04 in 2007.

s: In which year was the INSAT system commissioned?
x: The INSAT system was commissioned in 1983 with satellites procured abroad; the INSAT-2 series began in 1992.

s: KALPANA-1 holds which distinction in the Indian satellite programme?
o: First fully indigenous communication satellite series
First satellite for encrypted naval links
First commercial communication satellite in low Earth orbit
x: KALPANA-1 was India's first exclusive weather satellite.

s: Which satellite made the INSAT system operational in 1983?
x: INSAT-1A (1982) was the first INSAT, but INSAT-1B made the system operational in 1983.

s: Which body coordinates the INSAT system, a joint venture of DoS, DoT, IMD, AIR and Doordarshan?
x: The INSAT Coordination Committee (ICC) coordinates the system.

s: Which organisation took over ten in-orbit ISRO communication satellites in 2022?
x: NSIL took over 10 in-orbit communication satellites in 2022.

s:
Consider the following statements about KALPANA-1:
1. It was launched in September 2002 by PSLV.
2. It was also known as METSAT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: KALPANA-1 (METSAT) went up on PSLV in September 2002 as the first exclusive weather satellite.

s: Which satellite replaced INSAT-4C, which was lost in the GSLV-F02 failure of 10 July 2006?
x: After INSAT-4C was lost on GSLV-F02, ISRO launched INSAT-4CR in September 2007 on GSLV-F04.

s: How many operational communication satellites did India have in 2026?
x: India had 19 operational communication satellites in 2026; 10 in-orbit comsats were moved to NSIL in 2022.

s: Which of the following describes the Indian National Satellite (INSAT) system?
o: Combined communication and meteorological satellite system
x: INSAT serves both communication and meteorology from geostationary orbit (JPSC 2021 keyed it as a 'meteorological satellite'), and also carries broadcasting, disaster warning and search-and-rescue. It is not purely military, not a sun-synchronous remote-sensing system (that is IRS), and not a navigation system (that is NavIC).

s: The early-warning capability of INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR has had which of the following effects?
o: It sharply reduced cyclone-related deaths on the east coast, including Andhra Pradesh.
It provided encrypted naval communication up to 2,000 km from the coast.
It made BlueBird Block-2 the largest satellite in low Earth orbit.
It enabled the South Asian countries to opt out of satellite services.
x: INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR early warnings sharply reduced cyclone deaths along the east coast, including Andhra Pradesh.

s: By which launch vehicle was APPLE (1981), India's first experimental geostationary communication satellite, launched?
x: APPLE was launched in 1981 on Ariane-1 from Kourou. SLV-3 launched Rohini (1980); the Space Shuttle Challenger carried INSAT-1B (1983); the Vostok launcher carried IRS-1A (1988).

s: By which launch vehicle was INSAT-1B (1983), with which the INSAT system was commissioned, launched?
x: INSAT-1B went up on the US Space Shuttle Challenger; Ariane-1 carried APPLE (1981).

s: Which launch vehicle launched INSAT-4CR (2007), the heaviest satellite launched from India in its day?
x: INSAT-4CR (2,130 kg) was launched by GSLV-F04.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: INSAT-2 series – First fully indigenous INSAT series
x: INSAT-3D (2013) is an advanced meteorology satellite; the GAGAN payload is on GSAT-8.

s: Which is the heaviest communication satellite launched from Indian soil?
x: CMS-03/GSAT-7R (4,410 kg, LVM3-M5, Nov 2025) is the heaviest launched from India; GSAT-11 (~5.8 t) is the heaviest ISRO-built, launched abroad.

s: Which satellite is correctly matched with its principal use?
o: GSAT-6 — Large deployable antenna for mobile and strategic communication
GSAT-11 — First operational satellite of the INSAT system
x: GSAT-6, launched in 2015, has a large deployable antenna and supports mobile and strategic communication. GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7A serves the Air Force, and INSAT-1B marked operationalisation of INSAT.

s: Which is the heaviest ISRO-built satellite, weighing about 5.8 tonnes?
x: GSAT-11 is the heaviest ISRO-built satellite; CMS-03 is the heaviest launched from Indian soil.

s: Which payload is carried by GSAT-8, launched on Ariane-5 on 21 May 2011?
x: GSAT-8 carries the GAGAN payload (also on GSAT-10 and GSAT-15), not INSAT-3D.

s: For which purpose is EDUSAT (GSAT-3), launched in 2004 on GSLV-F01, dedicated?
x: EDUSAT is India's education satellite, located at 74°E.

s: What type of satellite is GSAT-30, launched on 17 January 2020 from Kourou, French Guiana?
x: GSAT-30 is a telecommunication satellite launched by Ariane from Kourou on 17 Jan 2020 (APPSC 2018 PYQ theme). Navigation is NavIC/NVS, earth observation is EOS/IRS, and the exclusive weather satellite was KALPANA-1.

s: Which satellite, launched in 2015, carries a large deployable antenna?
x: GSAT-6 (2015) is known for its large deployable antenna.

s: When was GSAT-30 launched from Kourou, French Guiana?
x: GSAT-30, a telecom satellite, went up from Kourou on 17 January 2020. 21 May 2011 was GSAT-8 and 6 February 2019 was GSAT-31.

s: In which year was GSAT-11, the heaviest ISRO-built satellite, launched?
x: GSAT-11 (about 5.8 t), the heaviest satellite built by ISRO, was launched from abroad in 2018.

s: Which launch vehicle launched the communication satellite CMS-01 from Sriharikota?
x: CMS-01 was launched by PSLV-C50 from Sriharikota.

s: What is the mass of CMS-03 (GSAT-7R), the heaviest communication satellite launched from Indian soil?
x: CMS-03 weighs 4,410 kg; GSAT-11 (about 5.8 t) is heavier but was launched abroad.

s: Besides GSAT-8, which satellites carry the GAGAN payload?
x: GAGAN payloads are on GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and GSAT-15.

s: From where was GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20) launched by Falcon 9 in November 2024?
x: GSAT-N2 flew on SpaceX's Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral.

s: From where was GSAT-31 launched on 6 February 2019?
x: GSAT-31 was launched on Ariane from Kourou, French Guiana.

s: Which of the following satellites was NOT launched on Ariane from Kourou?
x: GSAT-N2 was launched by Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral; the others flew on Ariane from Kourou.

s: On which rocket was GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20) launched in November 2024?
x: GSAT-N2 was launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral.

s: Which launch vehicle launched CMS-03 (GSAT-7R), which gives encrypted anti-jam naval links up to 2,000 km from the coast?
x: CMS-03/GSAT-7R was launched by LVM3-M5.

s: Which satellite was GSAT-30 (January 2020) launched to replace?
x: GSAT-30, a C/Ku communication satellite on Ariane-5, replaces INSAT-4A.

s:
Consider the following statements about satellite orbits:
1. A circular orbit is possible when centripetal force equals gravitational force.
2. An elliptical orbit has different apogee and perigee distances.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: a circular orbit needs centripetal force equal to gravity, and an elliptical orbit has unequal apogee and perigee.

s: At approximately what altitude is the International Space Station (ISS) located?
x: The ISS orbits at about 400 km, inside Low Earth Orbit. 36,000 km is geostationary height.

s: At about what height above the equator does a geostationary satellite orbit?
x: GEO is about 35,786 km above the equator with a 24-hour period; the height does not depend on the satellite's mass.

s: In which orbit does a launcher first place a geostationary satellite?
x: The launcher puts it in an elliptical GTO; the satellite's own motor then raises it to GEO.

s: What is an orbit whose apogee and perigee distances differ called?
x: An elliptical orbit has different apogee and perigee; a polar orbit is one that passes over the poles.

s: Which of the following is correct about the orbital height of a geostationary satellite?
o: Does not depend on the satellite's mass
Depends on the launch vehicle used
x: A geostationary satellite revolves at a fixed height that is independent of its mass.

s: GSAT-7A 'Angry Bird' (2018) is the dedicated satellite of which of the following?
x: GSAT-7A serves the Air Force; GSAT-7 'Rukmini' serves the Navy and GSAT-7B is proposed for the Army.

s: Which launch vehicle launched the South Asia Satellite (GSAT-9) in May 2017?
x: GSAT-9 flew on GSLV-F09 in May 2017; Pakistan opted out of it.

s: For which of the following is the proposed GSAT-7B meant?
x: GSAT-7 'Rukmini' serves the Navy, GSAT-7A the Air Force and GSAT-7B the Army.

s: Which country opted out of the South Asia Satellite (GSAT-9)?
x: The South Asia Satellite serves seven countries including Afghanistan, Maldives and Sri Lanka; Pakistan opted out.

s: Which launch vehicle launched GSAT-7 'Rukmini', the Navy's satellite, on 30 August 2013?
x: GSAT-7 flew on Ariane-5; CMS-03 (LVM3-M5) later replaced it.

s: Which satellite replaced GSAT-7 'Rukmini', the Indian Navy's communication satellite?
x: CMS-03 (GSAT-7R), launched in November 2025, replaced GSAT-7 for the Navy.

s: By which launch vehicle was GSAT-7 'Rukmini', the Indian Navy's communication satellite, launched in 2013?
x: GSAT-7 was launched by Ariane-5 from Kourou in 2013.

s: Which of the following sets contains only high-throughput or broadband satellites?
x: GSAT-19, GSAT-29, GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2 are identified with high-throughput broadband services for underserved areas, in-flight links and defence, complementing BharatNet.

s: Which satellite frequency band is typically used for DTH and VSAT?
x: Ku-band serves DTH and VSAT; C for telecom/TV distribution, Ka for high-throughput broadband and S for mobile satellite services.

s: Which one of the following frequency bands is NOT used for INSAT/GSAT satellite communication?
x: MF is not used in INSAT/GSAT communication (RPSC 2021). C/extended C serves telecom and TV distribution, Ku serves DTH and VSAT, and S serves mobile satellite services and the DWS downlink.

s: For what is the Ka band on GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2 used?
x: Ka band carries high-throughput broadband; Ku serves DTH/VSAT and S serves mobile services.

s: In the Disaster Warning System, which are the uplink and downlink bands respectively?
x: DWS warnings go up in C band and come down in S band to addressable coastal receivers.

s: High-throughput satellites such as GSAT-19, GSAT-29 and GSAT-11 support which programme?
x: The high-throughput Ka-band satellites GSAT-19, -29, -11 and N2 provide broadband capacity that supports BharatNet.

s: In satellite applications, what does MSS refer to?
x: MSS means mobile satellite services; DTH is Direct-to-Home broadcasting, VSAT business networks and DSNG satellite news gathering.

s: Through which satellite are Swayam Prabha's 40 free DTH education channels beamed?
x: Swayam Prabha uses GSAT-15 to provide 40 free Direct-to-Home education channels.

s: In the Disaster Warning System, cyclone warnings from the Cyclone Warning Centre at Chennai are
o: sent upward through S-band and received through C-band by all receivers without selection
sent upward through UHF and received through MF by television households
sent upward through C-band and received through S-band by selectively addressable receivers
sent upward through Ku-band and received through Ka-band only by military stations
x: The warning signal goes up on C-band and comes down on S-band to selectively addressable DWS receivers along the coast.

s: Under which international programme do INSAT's search-and-rescue transponders operate?
x: INSAT carries search-and-rescue transponders under the international COSPAS-SARSAT programme.

s: For what is DSNG, a satellite communication application, used?
x: DSNG is digital satellite news gathering.

s: With which of the following did Andhra Pradesh's RTGS sign an MoU in June 2025?
x: The RTGS–SHAR MoU was signed in June 2025; SDSC-SHAR also gives APSDMA cyclone-track data.

s:
Consider the following statements about satellite support for disaster management in Andhra Pradesh:
1. SDSC-SHAR provides cyclone-track data to APSDMA.
2. Satellite phones are used in emergencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: SHAR shares cyclone-track data with APSDMA and satellite phones are used in emergencies.

s: INSAT supports which search-and-rescue programme?
x: Besides telecom, TV, meteorology, telemedicine and tele-education, INSAT supports COSPAS-SARSAT search and rescue.

s: INSAT services are carried in which frequency bands?
x: INSAT uses the C, Ku, Ka and S bands; L5 and S are NavIC bands.

s: At about what inclination to the equator are NavIC's four inclined geosynchronous satellites placed?
x: NavIC has seven satellites: three in geostationary orbit and four in inclined geosynchronous orbit at about 29°.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NavIC signals and services?
o: The newer NVS satellites add a civilian L1 signal.
The original NavIC signals are broadcast in the L1 and L2 bands.
The Standard Positioning Service is open to all civilians, with accuracy better than 20 m.
The Restricted Service is the encrypted service.
x: Original NavIC signals are in the L5 and S bands; L1 and L2 are GPS signals.

s: Which organisation is the nodal authority for both NavIC and GAGAN?
o: Satellite Navigation Programme Office under ISRO
Directorate General of Civil Aviation alone
Ministry of Defence’s Integrated Defence Staff
x: The Satellite Navigation Programme Office under ISRO is the nodal authority for NavIC and GAGAN.

s: NavIC, a regional system unlike the global GPS, covers India and about how far beyond its borders?
x: NavIC is regional, covering India plus about 1,500 km beyond its borders, whereas GPS is global.

s: In which year did NavIC (formerly IRNSS) become fully operational?
x: NavIC became fully operational in 2018; navigation satellites have been launched since 2013. Its genesis lies in the Kargil (1999) GPS denial.

s: Which of the following is the composition of NavIC's seven-satellite constellation?
x: NavIC has 3 geostationary and 4 inclined geosynchronous satellites, not 4 + 3.

s: During which war did the US deny GPS data to India, leading to the need for an indigenous system like NavIC?
x: NavIC's genesis lies in the US denial of GPS data in the 1999 Kargil War.

s: In which bands does NavIC transmit its signals?
x: NavIC uses L5 and S; L1 and L2 are GPS signals (NVS satellites add civilian L1).

s: What is the full form of IRNSS, the earlier name of NavIC?
o: Integrated Regional Navigation and Surveillance System
Indian Range and Navigation Satellite System
x: IRNSS stands for Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System; it was renamed NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation).

s: What makes India's NavIC distinctive among developing countries?
o: the only system using both civilian and military signals
the only developing country operating a global navigation system
the only developing country with an independent regional navigation system
the first system jointly owned by India and the United States
x: India is described as the only developing country with its own independent regional navigation system.

s:
Consider the following statements about NavIC:
1. It has 4 GEO and 3 GSO satellites.
2. It uses the L5 and S bands.
3. It covers India and a region up to 1,500 km beyond it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NavIC uses the L5 and S bands and covers India + 1,500 km; it has 3 GEO and 4 GSO satellites, not 4 GEO and 3 GSO.

s: IRNSS/NavIC covers India and a region extending up to how far beyond it?
x: NavIC covers India plus 1,500 km, with 3 GEO + 4 GSO satellites, broadcasting in L5 and S bands.

s: Which of the following is the composition of the NavIC constellation?
x: NavIC has 7 satellites: 3 geostationary and 4 inclined geosynchronous.

s: At about what altitude do GPS satellites in the original design orbit?
x: GPS (US DoD, 1973) was designed with 24 satellites in 6 orbits at about 20,200 km; each circles the Earth twice a day.

s: An error of about one microsecond in an atomic clock used for positioning may produce a position error of about how much?
x: A one-microsecond clock error can produce an approximate position error of 300 metres, illustrating the importance of atomic clocks in navigation.

s: To which of the following does QZSS, a regional navigation satellite system, belong?
x: QZSS is Japan's regional system; Galileo (EU) is global.

s: BeiDou is the global navigation satellite system of which country?
x: BeiDou is China's global system.

s: How many satellites and orbits does the original GPS constellation have?
x: GPS was designed with 24 satellites in 6 orbits; NavIC has 7 satellites.

s: GLONASS is the satellite navigation system of which of the following?
x: GLONASS is Russia's; BeiDou is China's, Galileo the EU's and QZSS Japan's.

s: In which year was the GPS programme begun?
x: GPS (Global Positioning System) of the US Department of Defense was begun in 1973; its first satellite flew in 1978.

s: Which of the following global navigation satellite systems is under civilian control?
x: Galileo of the European Union, live since 2016, is under civilian control and works with GPS and GLONASS.

s: In which year did Europe's Galileo navigation system go live?
x: Galileo, the European Union's global navigation system, went live in 2016.

s: How many times a day does each GPS satellite go around the Earth?
x: GPS satellites orbit at about 20,200 km and circle the Earth twice a day.

s: To which country does QZSS, a regional satellite navigation system, belong?
x: QZSS (Japan) and NavIC (India) are regional; BeiDou is China's and GLONASS Russia's global system.

s: In which vehicles does MoRTH's AIS-140 rule make NavIC-enabled location trackers compulsory?
x: AIS-140 covers public transport vehicles, not all private cars; Snapdragon chipsets support NavIC.

s: Warnings about which of the following were broadcast to fishermen at sea by the reconfigured IRNSS-1A?
x: Reconfigured IRNSS-1A broadcasts cyclone, tsunami and high-wave warnings to fishermen at sea.

s: Which of the following GPS applications belongs to agriculture?
x: Precision farming is the agricultural use of GPS; fleet tracking, surveying and timing are GPS uses in other sectors.

s: Why is NavIC important for India's strategic autonomy?
o: In a conflict, Indian forces need not depend on foreign navigation systems
It provides global coverage like GPS
It uses the GPS L1 and L2 bands
x: An indigenous system frees forces and emergency responders from dependence on foreign navigation systems during conflict; NavIC is regional, uses L5 and S, and is run by ISRO.

s: Whose Snapdragon mobile chipsets support NavIC?
x: Qualcomm's Snapdragon chipsets support NavIC.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NavIC applications?
o: AIS-140 makes NavIC trackers compulsory in all private cars
Reconfigured IRNSS-1A sends cyclone and tsunami alerts to fishermen
It supports timing for Indian Standard Time
x: AIS-140 covers public transport vehicles only, not all private cars.

s: Elena Geo Systems is known for which of the following?
o: Supplying rubidium clocks for IRNSS satellites
Making Snapdragon chipsets that support NavIC
x: Elena Geo Systems made India's first NavIC-based device, used for precise directions on infrastructure projects.

s: Who developed the first NavIC-based device?
x: Elena Geo Systems built the first NavIC-based device.

s: What is the full form of GAGAN?
x: GAGAN stands for GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation.

s: What is the main function of a Satellite-Based Augmentation System?
o: replace every navigation satellite with a ground-based radar
broadcast real-time corrections for orbit, clock and ionospheric delay
increase satellite altitude without correcting navigation data
x: An SBAS broadcasts real-time corrections for orbit, clock and ionospheric delay, improving accuracy, integrity and availability.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about GAGAN?
o: It was jointly developed by ISRO and DRDO.
It serves the Indian Flight Information Region.
It supports precision approach and landing for civil aviation.
DGCA certified it for aviation approach guidance in 2015.
x: GAGAN was developed by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India, not DRDO.

s: GAGAN payloads are carried on GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and which other satellite?
x: GAGAN payloads are on GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and GSAT-15.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: MSAS is the SBAS associated with Japan. WAAS serves the USA and North America, EGNOS serves Europe and GAGAN serves India.

s: In which year did DGCA certify GAGAN for aviation approach guidance?
x: GAGAN was certified by DGCA for approach guidance in 2015.

s: EGNOS is the Satellite-Based Augmentation System of which region?
x: EGNOS serves Europe; WAAS serves the USA and GAGAN India.

s: Together with which organisation did ISRO develop GAGAN?
x: GAGAN is by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India, not DRDO.

s: Which region is served by MSAS, a Satellite-Based Augmentation System?
x: MSAS is Japan's SBAS; EGNOS is Europe's and WAAS is the USA's.

s: Besides communication payloads, GSAT-10 (2012) carried a payload for which system?
x: GSAT-10, launched on Ariane-5, carried communication and GAGAN payloads.

s: With which organisation does ISRO implement GAGAN?
x: GAGAN is an ISRO-Airports Authority of India system for civil aviation precision landing.

s: What does GAGAN stand for?
x: GAGAN = GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation; its ground stations send corrections for aviation.

s: A firm from which country supplied the rubidium clocks that repeatedly failed on first-generation IRNSS satellites?
x: They came from Swiss firm SpectraTime; ISRO switched to indigenous clocks in 2018.

s: After the last clock on IRNSS-1F failed on 13 March 2026, how many PNT-capable NavIC satellites remained?
x: Only IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I and NVS-01 remained PNT-capable - three satellites, below the four the service needs.

s: Which launch vehicle was used to launch the IRNSS-1 series satellites from Sriharikota?
x: All IRNSS satellites were launched from Sriharikota, and the IRNSS-1 series used PSLV launch vehicles.

s: Which launch vehicle launched NVS-01, the first navigation satellite with an indigenous rubidium atomic clock, in May 2023?
x: NVS-01 was launched in May 2023 on GSLV-F12 and was the first to carry an indigenous rubidium atomic clock; GSLV-F15 flew in January 2025.

s: The launch of NVS-02 in January 2025 was which milestone launch from Sriharikota?
x: NVS-02 (GSLV-F15) was the 100th Sriharikota launch; a valve glitch left it in the wrong orbit.

s: Which launch vehicle launched IRNSS-1A, India's first dedicated navigation satellite, on 1 July 2013?
x: IRNSS-1A flew on PSLV-C22; NVS-01 used GSLV-F12 and NVS-02 GSLV-F15.

s: How many navigation satellites has India launched since 2013?
x: Eleven navigation satellites have been launched since 2013, all from Sriharikota.

s:
Consider the following statements about NVS-02:
1. It was launched by GSLV-F15 in January 2025.
2. A valve glitch left it in the wrong orbit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: NVS-02 flew on GSLV-F15 in January 2025, and a valve glitch left it in the wrong orbit.

s: Which ISRO centre developed the indigenous atomic clocks that replaced the failed imported rubidium clocks of NavIC?
x: After the SpectraTime clocks failed, indigenous SAC clocks were used from 2018.

s: Why was the ecosystem of NavIC receivers thin at first?
o: L5 and S bands were not commonly included in mobile-phone chipsets
NavIC had no satellites in orbit
GPS prevented all receivers from using satellite signals
NavIC signals were transmitted only through optical fibre
x: Receiver adoption was constrained because L5 and S bands were not commonly supported in phone chipsets; the newer civilian L1 signal helps address this limitation.

s: Which combination best explains why NavIC could not fully replace GPS over India as reported in March 2026?
o: Absence of any regional coverage and lack of satellites since 1999
Excessive global coverage and too many civilian receivers
Repeated atomic-clock failures and the NVS-02 launch failure
Only the use of geostationary satellites, with no clock problems
x: Repeated atomic-clock failures and the NVS-02 launch failure reduced the effective constellation, preventing NavIC from fully replacing GPS over India.

s: Adding the civilian L1 band on NVS satellites helps NavIC overcome which limitation?
x: L5 and S are rarely in phone chips; adding L1 on NVS helps receivers adopt NavIC.

s:
Consider the following statements about NavIC's limitations:
1. It provides only regional coverage.
2. L5 and S bands are rarely found in phone chips.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: NavIC is regional, and its L5/S signals are rarely supported by phone chips.

s: Following the stoppage of the last rubidium atomic clock on IRNSS-1F on 13 March 2026, which one of the following describes NavIC's status?
o: Five PNT-capable satellites remained, enough for a position fix
All seven satellites lost navigation capability
Only three PNT-capable satellites remained, while a PNT fix needs at least four
IRNSS-1F was replaced the same week by NVS-02
x: After IRNSS-1F's last clock stopped (3 days after its 10-year design life), only IRNSS-1B, 1I and NVS-01 remained PNT-capable: three, below the minimum four needed. 'Five' and 'all seven lost' are wrong counts, and NVS-02 never reached its circular orbit (Jan 2025).

s:
Consider the following statements about NVS-02:
1. It was launched by GSLV-F14.
2. Its launch on 29 January 2025 was the 100th launch from Sriharikota.
3. A loose pyro connector was blamed for its failure to reach its circular orbit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NVS-02 was launched by GSLV-F15 (not F14) on 29 January 2025, the 100th Sriharikota launch; a loose pyro connector was blamed.

s:
Consider the following statements about SAR sensors:
1. SAR sensors can observe through clouds and in darkness.
2. SAR is an active sensor that uses its own microwave signal and reads the echo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: SAR sends its own microwave signal instead of relying on sunlight, so it works through clouds and in darkness.

s: For which of the following is hyperspectral remote sensing particularly useful?
o: Producing radar echoes from a single microwave band
Identifying materials or chemicals using hundreds of narrow spectral bands
Measuring only the revisit interval of a satellite
Determining satellite launch velocity without imaging
x: Hyperspectral sensing uses hundreds of narrow spectral bands, enabling identification of materials and their chemical characteristics.

s: Which of the following is a passive remote-sensing instrument?
x: Infrared radiometers record emitted heat and are passive; SAR and laser/LiDAR send their own pulse and are active.

s: What does optical (visible/near-infrared) imaging need?
x: Optical sensors use reflected light, so they need daylight and a clear sky, unlike SAR.

s: Which one of the following is an example of an active remote-sensing system?
x: LiDAR sends its own laser pulse and reads the echo, so it is active (APPSC 2023: laser is active). Multispectral cameras, infrared radiometers and visible cameras record sunlight reflected or heat emitted by the target, so they are passive.

s: Which of the following has the shortest wavelength?
x: In the electromagnetic spectrum, wavelength falls from infrared to visible to ultraviolet to gamma rays, so gamma rays have the shortest wavelength.

s: Which technique is most directly suited to detecting heat from volcanic eruptions, forest fires and urban heat?
x: Thermal infrared sensing records emitted heat and is therefore useful for volcanic eruptions, forest fires and urban heat mapping.

s: What was the former name of EOS-05, launched by GSLV-F17 on 4 September 2026?
x: EOS-05 was formerly GISAT-1A and became the first EO imager working from geosynchronous orbit; GISAT-1 was EOS-03.

s: Data from which satellite series is mainly used for Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories?
x: Oceansat supports PFZ advisories; Resourcesat serves crops and watersheds, Cartosat mapping and RISAT SAR imaging.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Oceansat — ocean colour and sea-surface temperature
x: HySIS is a hyperspectral-imaging satellite. Direct-to-home broadcasting is associated with communication satellites, not HySIS.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: SARAL — hyperspectral imaging of agricultural fields
x: SARAL is an ISRO-CNES altimetry mission using the AltiKa Ka-band altimeter to measure sea-surface height; hyperspectral agricultural imaging is associated with HySIS.

s: For what purpose was EOS-03, also known as GISAT-1, mainly intended?
o: Near-real-time geo-imaging of floods and cyclones
Measuring ocean winds for cyclone forecasting
x: EOS-03, formerly GISAT-1, was designed for geo-imaging and near-real-time observation of events such as floods and cyclones.

s: EOS-06 is the new name of which satellite?
x: EOS-06 is Oceansat-3 (used for PFZ advisories); EOS-04 is RISAT-1A.

s: A problem in which stage caused the failure of EOS-03 (GISAT-1), launched by GSLV-F10 in August 2021?
x: The EOS-03 mission failed due to a cryogenic-stage problem.

s: What does SCATSAT-1 measure with its scatterometer?
x: SCATSAT-1's scatterometer measures ocean wind vectors and helps track cyclones.

s: SARAL, carrying the AltiKa Ka-band altimeter, is a joint satellite of ISRO and which agency?
x: SARAL is an ISRO-CNES (France) satellite measuring sea-surface height.

s: EOS-04 is the new name of which satellite?
x: EOS-04 was RISAT-1A, a SAR satellite; GISAT-1 became EOS-03 and Oceansat-3 became EOS-06.

s: For what are Resourcesat satellites mainly used?
x: Resourcesat is for crops; Cartosat maps, Oceansat gives PFZ advisories and RISAT does radar imaging.

s:
Consider the following statements about EOS renamings:
1. EOS-03 was earlier GISAT-1.
2. EOS-05 was earlier GISAT-1A.
3. EOS-06 was earlier RISAT-1A.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: EOS-03 = GISAT-1 and EOS-05 = GISAT-1A; EOS-06 is Oceansat-3 (RISAT-1A is EOS-04).

s: For what is HySIS, an Indian satellite, used?
x: HySIS is a hyperspectral imaging satellite, not a DTH satellite.

s: In which year was Oceansat-1, India's first ocean satellite of the series, launched?
x: The Oceansat series began with Oceansat-1 in 1999.

s: Which is India's first geosynchronous land-imaging satellite?
x: EOS-05 is India's first geosynchronous land-imaging satellite; EOS-03 was lost at launch and the INSAT-3D series are weather satellites.

s: Which one of the following most appropriately describes remote sensing?
o: Preparation of maps only through manual surveying
Measurement of only the chemical composition of rocks by direct sampling
Recording of atmospheric pressure exclusively through ground instruments
Collection of information about the Earth without physical contact, using reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation
x: Remote sensing obtains information about the Earth without physical contact by detecting reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation.

s: In a remote sensing system, which stage comes right after recording by the sensor?
x: The stages run: energy source, atmosphere, interaction with target, recording, then transmission, reception and processing, interpretation, application.

s: Remote sensing gathers information about a target without which of the following?
x: Remote sensing works from a distance without physical contact, so physical sampling is not one of its stages.

s: Imagery from which satellite powers the KASTURI and Bharat Darshan heritage apps?
x: Cartosat-3 imagery (~25 cm resolution) powers KASTURI and Bharat Darshan; Cartosat-1 gave stereo images for 3D maps.

s: Which mission formed part of the record launch of 104 satellites into a 506 km sun-synchronous orbit on 15 February 2017?
x: The Cartosat-2 series was launched by PSLV-C37 on 15 February 2017 and formed part of the record 104-satellite launch into a 506 km SSO. Its mass was 714 kg.

s: What did Cartosat-1 (2005), India's first mapping satellite, provide?
x: Cartosat-1 gave stereo images for 3D maps; ~25 cm resolution is Cartosat-3.

s: Cartosat-3 was launched on PSLV-C47 along with how many US nanosatellites?
x: Cartosat-3 (Nov 2019) flew on PSLV-C47 with 13 US nanosatellites.

s: For which of the following is Cartosat-3 imagery used?
x: Cartosat-3 (~25 cm) supports Gati Shakti, borders and heritage apps.

s: In which year was Cartosat-1, India's first mapping satellite, launched?
